Prevention: Spodoptera pupae to natural enemies and weather- related factors.
Plant trap crops like sunflower, taro and castor around and within fields.
Apply balanced crop nutrition and don't overdose nitrogen for stronger plants that can better resist pest damage.
Enhance natural enemies by encouraging flowering plants near fields and by avoiding broad-spectrum insecticides.
Monitoring: Use para-pheromone traps (Spodolure) to monitor adults and to predict occurence of pest eggs.
Observe egg masses (covered with white-brown hair), and young larvae on leaves.
Observe for the presence of 'scratch' marks on the leaf surface made by newly hatched larvae.
Observe leaf damage caused by chewing/ stripping of large areas of the leaves in the field.
Direct Control: Collect and destroy egg masses and larvae based on the 'warning' from the pheromone traps.
Trichogramma chilonis @ 50,000 eggs/ha/week, for up to 6 weeks wherever available.
Nir 5 drops/L in the evening (25L water per ropani).
Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) @ 1g/L of water (25L of water per ropani).
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label.
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance.
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB).
Novaluron 10% EC @ 1 ml/L (25L water per ropani).
